description: Save the disposition reached about an artifact revision, with the basis it rests on: a list of requirement-checks, each saying where its requirement came from and what happened when it was checked. Re-remembering the same subject on the same artifact revision REPLACES that decision, which is how a decision is revised as the engineer answers questions or disagrees with a line. A different subject starts a separate decision, because one part can carry several at once. Record each engineer verdict when they have given one: a requirement the engineer accepted is a different thing from one that was proposed. Store each requirement as stated and each piece of evidence as it was reported. This server never opens or measures the artifact, so recall returns what was concluded, not a measurement — Geometry remains the authority for numbers.

revision.description: sha256 revision of the artifact, copied from a Geometry inspect result. It is the anchor every record is stored against, and recall compares it to mark records stale.

units.description: Spatial unit of the source file, echoed from inspect.

uri.description: Artifact location: a URI such as file:///parts/curved-sector.step, or a plain filesystem path such as /parts/curved-sector.step. Both address the same records, because a path is normalised to a file: URL before anything is stored against it. A relative path resolves against this server working directory. Records are grouped by it; without a URI the revision alone is the key.

basis.description: The requirement-checks the recommendation rests on.

evidence.description: The measured or computed value as it was reported, quoted with its provenance, e.g. "inspect: is_valid=true, face_count=5".

faces.description: Face IDs this item is about, valid only in the artifact revision below.

id.description: Stable within the decision. Use it again when revising this line.

note.description: One line of reasoning a reviewer needs when the state alone is not enough.

question.description: The question that would resolve this item. Required when the state is unresolved or conflicting.

requirement.description: What has to hold, stated so it can be checked.

source.description: Where the requirement comes from. Use assistant-proposed only for a requirement you raised yourself and the engineer has not yet made theirs.

sourceDetail.description: Clause, note number, document or spec name a reader can follow.

state.description: unresolved means the input needed to check it is missing; conflicting means two requirements or pieces of evidence disagree. Both are real outcomes.

verdict.description: The engineer's judgement on this line, when they have given one. Recording it is what makes a requirement agreed rather than merely proposed.

note.description: Why, when they gave a reason.

verdict.description: Whether the engineer accepted this line.

confidence.description: How much weight the evidence carries.

recommendation.description: The disposition, stated as a decision rather than a summary of the conversation.

status.description: Set 'confirmed' only once the engineer has accepted the disposition itself.

subject.description: What is being decided, in the engineer's words. Part of the record key: reuse the same subject to revise this decision, or a new subject starts a separate one.

supersedes.description: Revision whose decision for this subject this one replaces, when a part was revised.
